summary: When Queen Jezebel threatened Elijah, he ran away, exhausted and discouraged, and sat under a broom tree, wishing it was all over. An angel gave him food, water, and rest, twice.

story_reel.narration: After the amazing victory on Mount Carmel, you might think Elijah felt on top of the world. But when King Ahab told Queen Jezebel what happened, she sent Elijah a message: 'By this time tomorrow, I will get you!' Elijah was terrified. He ran for his life, all the way to Beersheba, and then another whole day's journey into the wilderness. Finally, he sat down under a broom tree, completely worn out. He was so tired, so scared, and so discouraged that he said, 'I've had enough, Yahweh. I can't do this anymore.' Then he lay down and fell asleep. Suddenly, an angel touched him and said, 'Get up and eat.' Elijah looked around, and there by his head was a warm loaf of bread baked on hot stones and a jar of water! He ate, drank, and lay down again. Then the angel of Yahweh came back a second time, touched him, and said, 'Get up and eat, because the journey is too much for you.' So Elijah ate and drank again. With the strength from that food, he traveled forty days and forty nights to Horeb, the mountain of God. God didn't scold Elijah for being tired and afraid. He gave him rest, food, and gentle care. Sometimes, when we're exhausted, the most spiritual thing we can do is eat, drink, and sleep.

scenes.caption: A threatening message
scenes.art_direction: Jezebel handing a scroll to a messenger with an icy stare.

scenes.caption: Running away
scenes.art_direction: Elijah running across the desert, looking over his shoulder.

scenes.caption: Under the broom tree
scenes.art_direction: Elijah slumped under a small desert tree, head in his hands; gray, heavy colors.

scenes.caption: 'Get up and eat'
scenes.art_direction: A gentle angel touching Elijah's shoulder; a warm loaf and a water jar beside him.

scenes.caption: A second time
scenes.art_direction: The angel returning as the sun rises; color slowly returning to the scene.

scenes.caption: Strength for the journey
scenes.art_direction: Elijah walking steadily toward a distant mountain.

memory_verse.text: Come to me, all you who labor and are heavily burdened, and I will give you rest.

identity_focus.core_truth: Yahweh cares for me gently when I'm tired, scared, or sad.
identity_focus.reflection_prompt: Elijah was so tired and sad, and God cared for him gently. When you feel really tired or sad, what helps you feel better?

quiz.question: Why did Elijah run away?
quiz.explanation: Jezebel sent a messenger to Elijah, and when he saw that, he arose and ran for his life.

quiz.question: What did the angel bring Elijah?
options: Bread baked on hot stones and a jar of water
quiz.explanation: There was at his head a cake baked on the coals, and a jar of water.

quiz.question: How long did Elijah travel after eating?
quiz.explanation: He went in the strength of that food forty days and forty nights to Horeb, the mountain of God.

micro_prayer.text: Yahweh, thank You for caring for me when I'm tired, scared, or sad. Help me come to You for rest. When I feel really low, help me tell a grown-up I trust. Amen.

companion.message: Even great heroes like Elijah get exhausted and discouraged. If you ever feel really sad or like you can't go on, please tell a grown-up you trust right away. You matter so much.

review.notes: Sensitive: Elijah asks to die (1 Kings 19:4), softened to 'I've had enough... I can't do this anymore.' Companion directs kids to a trusted grown-up. Reviewer should consider linking to parent resources on childhood sadness and depression. Confirm.
